children: ING Groep launched a stock buyback of 1.65 billion euros, equivalent to $1.84 billion, as it set out plans to restructure its wholesale banking unit and make 400 redundancies.
The Dutch bank's buyback program was larger than the 1.25 billion-euro plan analysts expected. ING said a further 250 million euros will be paid out in cash to shareholders in January.

ING said it is creating a more streamlined structure for its wholesale banking business, which serves large corporates and financial institutions. The changes--which will become effective in March--will lead to around 400 redundancies, ING said. The bank has more than 60,000 employees, according to its website.
It will also change the unit's name to corporate and institutional banking to better reflect its focus.

"As a reliable banking partner, we aim to create greater value for our clients and all our stakeholders. We will create a more streamlined structure which supports closer relationships with clients, to serve them with more impact and relevance," the bank said.
ING anticipates the measures to result in a cost reduction of around 75 million euros a year, fully effective from 2028 onward.
It expects to book a 175 million-euro pretax redundancy provision in the fourth quarter.

ING joins a swathe of banks that have downsized as part of structural reorganizations, resulting in thousands of job cuts worldwide. Last week, Barclays said it will cut around 5,000 roles, or 5% of its workforce, as it adopts artificial intelligence across the bank.
Germany's Commerzbank and Norway's DNB have also outlined plans to shed jobs this year.

ING on Thursday posted net profit of 1.85 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 1.79 billion euros a year ago. The print was below analysts' expectations of 1.97 billion euros, according to a consensus of estimates provided by the bank.
Total income came in 5.6% higher at 6.23 billion euros but was lower than the consensus estimate of 6.31 billion euros.
ING said lower other income due to increased interest rate volatility partly offset commercial interest income and fee income growth.
"We enter the remainder of this year with good momentum and continued customer growth," said Chief Executive Officer Steven van Rijswijk.
The bank reaffirmed its outlook for both 2026 and 2027. It expects total income to exceed 24.5 billion euros this year, and to grow to more than 26 billion euros next year.
